title: WBTC vault types are retained in the Atlas purely for Stability Fee consistency while being excluded from the Native Vault Engine
content:
A.3.7.1.1.3.2 states that "WBTC-A, WBTC-B and WBTC-C are defined in A.3.7.1.1.1 - Vault Types only for the purpose of Stability Fee consistency. These are otherwise not considered Native Vault Engine collateral and should be offboarded according to A.3.7.1.1.3.3 - Offboarding Other Collateral."

The parameter tables confirm the in-between status: all three WBTC types carry a DC-IAM `line` of 0 Dai — no new debt can be created — and a Liquidation Penalty (`chop`) of 0%, the penalty setting A.3.7.1.5.2.1 prescribes for collateral already being offboarded. They are wind-down positions, not live products.

The consequence is a definitional split worth flagging for anyone reasoning from the Atlas structurally: membership in the Vault Types document does *not* imply membership in the Native Vault Engine. Rules that key off "Native Vault Engine collateral" — including the mandatory 20-million offboarding trigger in A.3.7.1.1.3.1 — do not reach WBTC, which instead falls under the discretionary "when the Core Facilitator deems it appropriate" route.

The carve-out is defensible (WBTC positions still accrue fees, and their fee levels should stay coherent with comparable collateral) but it means the same list serves two purposes, and a reader must consult A.3.7.1.1.3.2 to know which entries are real.
description: A.3.7.1.1.3.2 keeps WBTC-A/B/C listed among Vault Types yet declares them not Native Vault Engine collateral, to be offboarded under the discretionary route.
